We show that this constraint can be circumvented even in the non-red-sideband regime via tunneling-coupling-induced mode splitting and engineering the cavity linewidth to boost scattering probability, thereby overcoming the weak-pump limitation. A directional optical parametric amplifier further enables efficient Lorentz reciprocity violation. Our approach establishes a versatile platform for chip-scale nonreciprocal vector optomechanical devices, such as isolators and circulators-free from the stringent frequency-matching requirements of traditional schemes.

title: Beam-based approach to verify nuclear hyperfine mixing effect
abstract: Electromagnetic coupling between a nucleus and its bound electron(s) can induce mixing of nuclear levels—a phenomenon known as nuclear hyperfine mixing (NHM). This effect can greatly enhance light-nucleus interactions and is expected to play a key role in laser-based nuclear control. Although predicted in 1966, NHM has not yet been experimentally confirmed. Here we propose a beam-based scheme to test the NHM effect via collisions between hydrogenlike 229 Th ions ( 229 Th 89+ ) and a thin-layer target. This approach avoids the need for resonance tuning and enables detection of prompt ultraviolet photons as a clear experimental signature of NHM. To evaluate the excitation probability of the nuclear isomeric state, we develop, for the first time, nuclear excitation theories that incorporate NHM in both electron- and nucleus-induced processes.

title: High-pressure tuning of electrical transport in freestanding iridates across dimensions
abstract: Flexible control of crystalline dimensionality and pressure is highly desirable for discovering emergent phenomena but has rarely been achieved within a single oxide. Here we develop a high-pressure strategy that enables pressure to be applied to most freestanding oxide thin films. Using this approach, we uncover a pressure-driven semimetal-insulator-metal transition in three-dimensional iridates and a pressure-robust insulating state in the two-dimensional limit. First-principles calculations reveal that the contrasting pressure responses arise from fundamentally different pressure evolutions of the effective electron correlation. While the correlation strength decreases systematically with pressure in two dimensions, it evolves nonmonotonically in three dimensions, first increasing and then decreasing under compression. Our work opens new opportunities to explore dimensionality effects in the pressure response of quantum materials.

title: Initialization-free ultralow-power programmable spin-orbit torque logic devices enabled by chirally asymmetric switching
abstract: Spin logic is of great interest for the development of high-performance, non-Von Neumann artificial intelligence chips. Of particular advantage is the programmable spin-orbit torque logic that can achieve the complete set of the 16 Boolean logic operations within a single device in an initialization-free, low-power, and scalable manner, which is, however, a challenge despite remarkable efforts over more than two decades. Here, utilizing chirally asymmetric switching, we demonstrate an initialization-free, low-power, programmable spin-orbit torque logic device that is capable of the complete set of 16 Boolean logic operations within a single device with only three inputs and ultralow power of < 1 fJ/bit. We also propose the first initialization-free, all-electrical spin-based cascading computing devices, including a half adder, a three-level full adder, a two-level full adder, and a Transfer/NOT selector. These compact and scalable computing devices are enabled by the chirally asymmetric spin-orbit torque switching of a Ta/FeCoB bilayer with a significant perpendicular Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction field. These results pave an intriguing way for the development of next-generation high-performance large-scale in-memory computing chips based on chirally asymmetric spin-orbit torque switching.

title: Efficient terahertz emission from a single-layer ferromagnet via co-existing spin and charge conversion
abstract: Optically pumped spintronic terahertz (THz) emitters based on ferromagnetic/nonmagnetic (FM/NM) heterostructures present a promising scheme for broadband, low-cost THz generation. However, their efficiency is fundamentally limited by interfacial spin transmission losses, and their dependence on external magnetic fields complicates device integration and miniaturization. Here, we report a paradigm shift in emitter design by demonstrating an efficient, field-free, broadband THz emitter based on a single-layer ferromagnetic alloy. By utilizing chemically disordered, face-centered cubic Fe x Pt 1− x , we integrate spin current generation and conversion within a single material layer, thereby circumventing the interfacial spin memory loss inherent to traditional bilayer structures. Crucially, the asymmetry at the film’s interfaces enables a net longitudinal current, which is then converted into a transverse THz current by the bulk anomalous Hall effect (AHE) and inverse spin Hall effect (ISHE). The optimized A1-phase Fe 50 Pt 50 composition exhibits a THz emission peak amplitude 1.52 times greater than that of a standard 1-mm-thick ZnTe crystal. This work establishes a simplified, robust, and efficient platform for ultrabroadband THz generation, paving the way for practical applications in spectroscopy, imaging, and nonlinear optics.

title: Thermodynamic scaling laws and ionization kinetics of laser-produced tin plasmas at various pressures and irradiating laser energies
abstract: Laser-produced tin plasmas are fundamental to extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography, yet optimizing their emission efficiency requires precise empirical boundary conditions for high-fidelity radiation-hydrodynamics simulations. In this study, the ionization kinetics and thermodynamic scaling laws of solid-Sn laser-produced plasmas were systematically investigated using quantitative optical emission spectroscopy (OES), by extracting the electron temperature ( T e ) and electron density ( N e ) under varying incident laser energies and ambient pressures. Results reveal that in a controlled low-pressure environment of 50 mbar, the plasma efficiently couples with the laser, exhibiting a robust power-law scaling of T e ∝ E 0.43 , close to the theoretical 4/9 limit of the classical self-regulating regime. In contrast, atmospheric confinement severely suppresses this scaling to E 0.27 due to prominent plasma shielding and plasma-gas interactions. Furthermore, the electron density evolution demonstrates a distinct two-stage ionization mechanism, transitioning to dominant electron avalanche ionization above a 110 mJ threshold. Statistical analysis confirms that low-pressure conditions effectively suppress macroscopic hydrodynamic instabilities, minimizing single-shot T e fluctuations to below 0.05 eV. These results establish a reproducible spectroscopic dataset and quantitative scaling framework for benchmarking radiation-hydrodynamics models of solid-Sn laser-produced plasmas relevant to EUV source development.

title: Quantum biology, quantum simulation and quantum coherent devices
abstract: Many living organisms can exploit quantum mechanical effects to gain distinct biological advantages. In plants, photosynthesis uses quantum coherence to achieve near 100% efficiency in energy transfer. With advances in experimental techniques, two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy can reveal dynamic processes such as coherence and coupling within a system, and it plays an important role in studying energy transfer in photosynthesis. On the theory side, methods such as the generalized Bloch-Redfield theory and the hierarchical equations of motion are used to model photosynthetic systems. Quantum simulation, as a high-efficiency and low-complexity approach, has also made progress across various platforms in the study of photosynthesis. In recent years, a series of studies has introduced quantum coherence into artificial systems to enhance energy transfer efficiency, laying the groundwork for the design of coherent devices with efficient energy transport. Birds can use the weak geomagnetic field and spin-dependent chemical reactions to detect direction. Theoretical frameworks for animal navigation include magnetite-based mechanisms, magnetoreceptor genes, and the radical-pair mechanism. Quantum simulations of navigation have also advanced on multiple platforms. Inspired by animal navigation, diverse quantum effects have been applied to improve sensing and to support navigation tasks. This paper presents a comprehensive review of progress on quantum coherence in photosynthesis and avian navigation, along with related theoretical methods, quantum simulation approaches, and research on quantum coherent devices.

title: Visualizing modified spin-wave wavefronts near magnetic defects and domains using nitrogen-vacancy centers
abstract: Direct, real-space imaging of spin-wave propagation and wavefronts in magnetic materials is crucial for advancing both fundamental understanding of spin dynamics and the development of functional devices. This, however, remains a significant challenge, especially in materials with complex magnetic characteristics at the nanoscale. Here, we employ scanning nitrogen-vacancy center spectroscopy to achieve visualization of spin waves in two archetypical magnetic films: yttrium-iron-garnet and lanthanum strontium manganese oxide. We reveal a wavelength-dependent spin-wave filtering effect near point-like magnetic scatterers and a modified spin wavefront in antiferromagnetically coupled stripe domains. The spin-wave characteristics are explained using micromagnetic simulations and analytical calculations. These findings point to possible fine control of spin-wave propagation near complex magnetic structures and extend the scope of spin-wave imaging based on nitrogen-vacancy centers beyond uniform magnets.

title: Learning parton fragmentation with QCD built in
Spin polarization and quantum entanglement of baryon-antibaryon pairs produced in electron-positron annihilation
abstract: In this work, we systematically investigate the evolution of spin polarization and quantum entanglement in cascade decays of baryon-antibaryon pairs, which are produced in electron-positron annihilation. We derive a fully analytical spin density matrix explicitly expressed in terms of spin polarization observables, extend this formalism to multi-step cascade decay scenarios, and establish compact recursive relations to facilitate density matrix calculations for such processes. It is found that when maximal parity violation occurs during a decay, the resulting final-state particles are fully polarized and exist in a non-entangled state. Furthermore, we demonstrate that quantum entanglement amplification is a generic characteristic of charge-conjugate decays under $CP$ conservation when the initially produced baryon-antibaryon pair is polarized.

title: Constraints on axion-like particles with the silicon detector at a nuclear reactor
abstract: Axion and axion-like particles (ALPs), predicted in various extensions of the Standard Model, can be abundantly produced in nuclear reactors via the Primakoff process. In this work, we explore the detection of ALPs in silicon detectors through plasmon excitations. Owing to their relativistic nature, reactor-produced ALPs can efficiently excite plasmon resonances, while the accompanying energetic photon typically escapes from the thin detector without depositing an appreciable amount of energy. Utilizing the data from the Connie and Atucha-II experiments, we set the 90\% confidence level upper limits on the ALP-photon coupling $g_{aγγ}$ over the axion mass range $0.1-100$ keV. We further show that, for an exposure of 30 kg$\cdot$yr, the projected sensitivity of vIOLETA exceeds the current NEON limit by a factor of three in the same mass range. This improvement would expand the explored region of the QCD axion and ALP parameter space.

title: Two routes for quantum AI in nonlinear dynamics
Parton fragmentation functions extracted with a physics-informed neural network
abstract: Reliable predictions of many high-energy strong interaction processes rely heavily on the non-perturbative parton fragmentation functions (FFs) extracted from existing experimental data. Conventional methods often require parameterized forms of FFs and additional scale evolution according to the Dokshitzer-Gribov-Lipatov-Altarelli-Parisi (DGLAP) evolution equations. We introduce a novel approach to determining parton FFs using a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN). Unlike traditional methods, our approach does not require prior parameterized forms and directly integrates the DGLAP evolution equations into the neural network architecture, allowing the FFs to automatically satisfy these equations. We present new sets of parton FFs extracted from hadron spectra in electron-positron annihilation processes at next-to-leading order (NLO) in pQCD using this new technique. To validate our approach, we calculate charged hadron spectra in proton-(anti)proton collisions using the extracted FFs and demonstrate that the results align well with experimental data across a large range of colliding energies ($\sqrt{s}$ = 130, 200, 500, 630, 900, 1800, 2760, 5020, 5440, 7000 GeV). Our findings indicate that the PINN method not only simplifies the extraction process but also enhances the universal applicability of FFs across different energy scales. By eliminating the need for parameterized forms and additional DGLAP evolution, our approach represents a significant step forward toward fast and accurate extractions of non-perturbative quantities such as parton fragmentations functions and parton distribution functions.

title: Flash DSC: Unlocking non-equilibrium phase transitions in glassy materials
When symmetry protects spectroscopy in interacting many-body systems
Towards nonadiabatic geometric quantum computation with bosonic binomial codes
Probing gravitational quantum field theory through polarization fingerprints of gravitational waves
abstract: Gravitational Quantum Field Theory (GQFT) has been proposed as a candidate framework to reconcile general relativity with quantum field theory, and a distinctive imprint on gravitational-wave (GW) polarizations is crucially predicted. While general relativity allows only two tensor modes ($+, \times$), GQFT additionally favors a massless breathing scalar mode, providing a compelling yet largely unexplored observational target for testing quantum gravity. The central challenge is therefore to assess, in a mission-agnostic manner, how well future space-based interferometers can disentangle and detect these tensor and scalar polarization components across the sky. In this work, we develop a model-independent response formalism for LISA- and Taiji-like detectors by incorporating first-order orbital dynamics in the Solar System Barycenter frame. This framework yields three key observational consequences: (1) characteristic interference patterns between tensor and scalar modes, (2) a generalized, model-independent response function for the breathing mode, and (3) sky-position-dependent strategies that optimize detectability. We further translate the formalism into comprehensive polarization maps that provide complete sky coverage and remain fully compatible with existing mission designs, thereby circumventing the need for challenging direct breathing-mode measurements. Overall, our results deliver practical tools for future data analysis and establish a systematic avenue to test fundamental theories of gravity through their GW polarization fingerprints.

title: Linear-in-T resistivity from van Hove singularity
Discovery of massive three-dimensional periodic orbits for the general three-body problem
abstract: Periodic orbits form the organizing skeleton of phase space in the three-body problem. While planar periodic solutions have been extensively studied, three-dimensional configurations remain comparatively scarce due to their increased complexity. Here we report the discovery of 10,059 three-dimensional periodic orbits of the three-body problem with two or three equal masses. The solutions span a diverse array of families, including spatial Lagrange, Sitnikov-like, Broucke-Hadjidemetriou-Hénon (BHH), and figure-8, as well as many sequences with more intricate topologies. Notably, approximately 20% (1,996) of these orbits are linearly stable, suggesting that they could arise in dense stellar systems. We further highlight two novel classes: 21 choreographic orbits for the three-equal-mass case, where all three bodies share a single closed 3D trajectory; and 273 “piano-trio” orbits, where the two equal masses share one closed loop while the third body follows a distinct path. We also demonstrate that these periodic orbits can be numerically continued to systems in which all three masses are distinct. These results provide a broad 3D atlas of periodic solutions and advance the global characterization of three-body dynamics.

title: Beyond backpropagation: Monte Carlo method can train deep neural networks
abstract: Backpropagation (BP) dominates deep learning training, but its reliance on gradients brings inherent troubles—vanishing and exploding gradients. The pursuit of gradient-free methods has long been a goal in the field of artificial intelligence. This paper shows that indeed the simplest Monte Carlo algorithm implemented on a single GPU—randomly mutate a parameter, keep it if the loss decreases, otherwise retry—can practically train deep networks. This gradient-free method does not even need common techniques such as batch normalization or residual connections to directly train sufficiently deep networks. More remarkably, its flexibility extends to several nontrivial scenarios: it enables pure pruning training, supports discrete weights, accommodates unconventional transfer functions such as Gaussian, and reveals the substantial redundancy of deep networks. We have demonstrated its feasibility on deep networks with more than 20 layers, single-hidden-layer wide networks with up to 16384 hidden neurons, and even a simple Transformer architecture trained on both image classification (MNIST) and character-level language modeling (Tiny Shakespeare). This simple gradient-free method may offer a complementary perspective for understanding the self-organization and learning mechanisms of neural networks, and also provides an alternative route for building physically inspired deep learning systems.

title: MUltiplexed Survey Telescope (MUST) science white paper I: Overview of large-scale structure cosmology in the era of Stage-V spectroscopic surveys
abstract: The MUltiplexed Survey Telescope (MUST) is a 6.5-m telescope under development. Dedicated to highly-multiplexed, wide-field spectroscopic surveys, MUST observes over 20000 targets simultaneously using 6.2-mm pitch positioning robots within a ∼5 deg 2 field of view. MUST aims to conduct the first Stage-V spectroscopic survey in the 2030s, mapping the 3D Universe with over 100 million galaxies and quasars, spanning from the nearby Universe to a redshift of z ∼ 5.5, corresponding to approximately 1 billion years after the Big Bang. To cover this extensive redshift range, we present an initial conceptual target-selection algorithm for different types of galaxies, including local bright galaxies, luminous red galaxies, emission-line galaxies, and high-redshift (2 < z < 5.5) Lyman-break galaxies. Using Fisher forecasts, we demonstrate that MUST can address fundamental questions in cosmology, including the nature of dark energy, tests of gravity theories, and investigations into primordial physics. This is the first paper in a series of science white papers for MUST, with subsequent papers focusing on additional scientific cases, including galaxy and quasar evolution, Milky Way physics, and dynamic phenomena in the time-domain Universe.

title: Tailoring light emission in hybrid WS2 monolayer-coupled polystyrene microsphere/Au microcavities
abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) monolayers provide a versatile platform for nanophotonic and optoelectronic devices due to their direct bandgap and strong excitonic response. However, tailoring their emission characteristics beyond the intrinsically narrow excitonic linewidth remains a key challenge. Here, we report a hybrid microcavity platform consisting of a WS 2 monolayer coupled to polystyrene microspheres (PS-MSs) on a gold substrate under continuous-wave excitation. In this system, light emission can be tailored through the interplay between cavity-enhanced local electromagnetic fields and photoinduced changes in the microcavity optical response. At low excitation powers, the emission evolves from neutral-exciton-dominated to trion-dominated photoluminescence with a continuously tunable intensity ratio, reflecting changes in the relative exciton-trion contributions under laser excitation. At higher excitation powers, the system transitions to a broadband-emission regime, which is associated with irradiation-induced modifications of the microcavity optical properties and is further enhanced by the cavity configuration. The incorporation of the WS 2 monolayer is correlated with enhanced broadband emission and improved performance under continuous-wave excitation, while also influencing the interfacial excitonic emission behavior. Furthermore, extending this approach to multiple-microsphere assemblies enables larger-area broadband emission, suggesting the potential scalability of this strategy toward planar white-light sources. These results establish a simple strategy for tailoring light emission in hybrid microcavities and provide insights into cavity-enhanced optical processes in coupled two-dimensional material-polymer systems, with potential applications in integrated photonic devices and broadband light sources.

title: Pressure meets dimensionality in freestanding iridate membranes
The sinking statistics of dark matter subhalos across hierarchical levels
abstract: We investigate the mergers among subhalos in a ΛCDM simulation, focusing on two fundamental aspects overlooked by previous studies: (1) how to identify mergers robustly; (2) the statistics of mergers across the subhalo hierarchy. To this end, we make use of the hbt + subhalo finder that tracks subhalo evolution across hierarchy levels, identifying the coalescence of subhalo cores in phase space as a “sinking” event. This coalescence marks a distinct stalled phase in orbital decay, providing a physically motivated and natural definition of a resolved merger. Moreover, the phase transition occurs over a very short timescale, making the statistics robust to numerical resolution. Our main findings are as follows. (1) More than 90% of sinking events occur between adjacent subhalo levels, while cross-level pathways arise from tidal stripping, group accretion, and numerical constraints. (2) Resolved sinking events are predominantly major mergers (mass ratios > 1:10), whereas the contribution from minor mergers decreases with the dynamical age of the host halo. (3) Although deep-level subhalos typically have low mass ratios relative to the host halo, their mass ratios relative to their direct parents are substantially larger, significantly enhancing their sinking probability. Consequently, the satellite-satellite sinking rate can rival or even exceed the central-satellite sinking rate at lower mass thresholds. (4) Satellite-satellite sinking events are spatially biased toward the outer regions of the host halo, suggesting that the central tidal field suppresses orbital decay between satellite systems.

title: Superconductivity of bilayer two-orbital Hubbard model for La3Ni2O7 under high pressure
abstract: By combining density functional theory (DFT) and density matrix renormalization group calculations, we investigate the unusual pressure dependence of superconducting transition temperature ( T c ) in the nickelate superconductor La 3 Ni 2 O 7 . Using the parameters obtained by fitting the DFT results, we map a quantum phase diagram of a bilayer two-orbital Hubbard model with increasing pressure. Near 3/8-filling, we find a strong spin density wave (SDW) order, which at 3/8-filling shows a real-space pattern similar to the spin-charge stripe order. At 21/64-filling, we find a superconducting phase with interlayer superconductivity (SC) in both the \(d_{z^{2}}\) and \(d_{x^{2}-y^{2}}\) orbitals, as well as in-plane SC in the \(d_{z^{2}}\) orbital. Intriguingly, the SC is weakened with increasing pressure and transitions to a Luttinger liquid above 80 GPa, which qualitatively agrees with the experimental observations of decreasing T c with increasing pressure and a transition to a Fermi liquid above 80 GPa. We further show that the ratio of interaction to hopping integral, which reduces moderately with increasing pressure, may play a dominant role in the weakening of SC. Our results not only find a robust SC through suppressing the competing SDW order, but also give new insight into the unusual pressure dependence of SC in La 3 Ni 2 O 7 .

title: Growth from KiDS: Stellar mass assembly of galaxies since z=2 in the light of Kilo-Degree Survey
abstract: We measure the galaxy stellar mass function (GSMF) at z = 0–2 using 28 million galaxies from the KiDS DR4, which spans an effective survey area of 676.9 deg 2 . Combining nine-band photometry ( u – K s ) and redshifts derived using deep learning photometry, we use five SED fitting configurations: CIGALE (combined with delayed exponential declining star formation history)/LePhare (combined with exponential declining star formation history) and CB19/BC03/M05 stellar population synthesis (SPS). We present the impact of the systematics related to the code, SPS modeling and star formation history (SFH), which combined can introduce systematics of ∼0.6 dex. The GSMFs outlined in this work agree well with previous studies (within the uncertainties introduced by systematics) that typically are able to cover measurements for the GSMF only up to log( M * / M ⊙ ) ∼ 11.75, due to their limited volume. The large KiDS area and galaxy counts, allow us to gain some insights on the “extreme” high-mass end, and our GSMFs imply that possibly there are more massive galaxies than we would expect, from a simple exponential cut-off, at log( M * / M ⊙ ) > 11.75. However, we heed caution that, despite advances done both in redshift estimation techniques and SPS, future studies are required to confirm this behavior. We consider the effects of Eddington bias (EB) to our observations via two different methods and compare our results with the predictions of semi-analytic models and hydrodynamical simulations. We use the mean absolute difference (MAD) of residuals as a diagnostic metric. Due to inconsistencies (> 0.5 dex) between observations and Eddington-biased simulations found, especially at the high-mass end, we suggest that some theoretical models would achieve better performance once parameter tuning takes into account the effects of EB prior to the tuning of the uncertain parameters involved related to stellar physics and feedback.

title: Prospects for probing supermassive binary black holes in strongly lensed active galactic nuclei via microlensing effects
abstract: Gravitational microlensing in strongly lensed active galactic nuclei (AGNs) provides a powerful probe of accretion-disk structure and may offer a unique opportunity to identify sub-parsec supermassive binary black holes (SMBBHs) through distinctive signatures. Upcoming wide-field surveys are expected to discover a large sample of strongly lensed AGNs, a fraction of which may host SMBBHs detectable via microlensing. In this paper, we employ semi-analytic models to assess the detection prospects of sub-parsec SMBBHs in lensed AGNs, focusing on systems with resolvable multiple images suitable for microlensing analysis. Accounting for galaxy-scale strong-lensing statistics, and including the cluster-lensing contribution as an optimistic statistical extension, we estimate that up to approximately 87 such systems could be spatially resolved by individual upcoming surveys, including the Vera C. Rubin Observatory (Rubin), Euclid, China’s Space Survey Telescope (CSST), and the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope (Roman). For the Rubin Wide-Fast-Deep survey, we estimate that periodic oscillations in microlensing light curves could identify ∼0.12–0.68 short-period (<5 yr) binaries, whereas diagnostics based on the reconstructed size-wavelength relation apply to a broader population, potentially identifying ∼0.4–5.3 systems, depending on the model assumptions. CSST, Euclid, and Roman may also reveal up to 10.6, 8.9, and 1.2 systems exhibiting size-wavelength features, and 2.3, 1.9, 0.3 systems showing periodic oscillations, which should be regarded as imaging-selected candidates whose microlensing-based identification requires adequate time-domain follow-up, including cadence, monitoring baseline, photometric precision, and reliable time-delay measurements. Our results show that strongly lensed AGNs provide a promising, though observationally demanding, pathway for finding candidate SMBBHs via microlensing.

title: Evolution of magnetic interactions across triangular-lattice Ce-based chalcogenides
abstract: Realizing quantum spin liquids (QSLs) in real materials requires understanding how crystal structure dictates magnetic interactions. The triangular-lattice family KCe Ch 2 ( Ch = O, S, Se) offers an ideal platform to investigate this link, as anion substitution alone (O → S → Se) drives a magnetic crossover from AFM-120° to stripe- yz order—signaling a systematic reconstruction of the underlying exchange interactions. Combining inelastic neutron scattering (INS) and thermodynamic measurements with linear spin-wave (LSW) theory and exact diagonalization (ED), we determine the anisotropic exchange parameters for the full series. By mapping these parameters onto the J-K-Γ-Γ′ phase diagram via density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) calculations, we find that KCeO 2 lies within the AFM-120° region, close to the boundary with stripe order. Isovalent substitution is widely employed as a materials strategy to tune exchange interactions toward QSL. However, the substitution from O to S to Se acts through two synergistic effects: the decreasing ligand electronegativity suppresses J and ∣ Γ ∣, while the reduction of the local octahedral distortion enhances ∣ K ∣ and suppresses ∣ Γ′ ∣. This coupled evolution forces the system directly from AFM-120° to stripe- yz order, bypassing the QSL. Our DMRG analysis further identifies this QSL as a gapped state with short-range spin correlations, consistent with the strong spin-orbit coupling that breaks continuous spin-rotation symmetry. These results establish that anion substitution alone is insufficient to access the QSL in this family, and that realizing this state requires decoupling the magnetic anisotropy from the structural evolution.

title: Beyond the plane: A massive atlas of three-dimensional periodic orbits in the general three-body problem
Spectral butterfly effect and resilient ringdown in thick braneworlds
abstract: The quasinormal mode spectrum is a unique fingerprint linking gravitational-wave observations to extra-dimensional geometry. In this article, we show that thick braneworlds exhibit a spectral butterfly effect: infinitesimal deformations of the effective potential trigger dramatic migrations of quasinormal modes, challenging the presumed stability of this fingerprint. Frequency-domain instabilities depend sensitively on the perturbation’s location and strength. In the time domain, near-brane perturbations primarily modify the early ringdown, while far-brane perturbations generate clean late-time echoes. Crucially, the graviton zero mode remains localized, preserving four-dimensional gravity. Despite this pronounced spectral fragility, the observable early-stage signal under current detector sensitivities is still dominated by the original fundamental mode. Hence, thick braneworlds display a nontrivial coexistence of a fragile spectrum and a resilient ringdown, supporting the continued use of the standard fingerprint in present-day gravitational-wave astronomy while revealing its hidden sensitivity.

title: Autler-townes energy-level engineering for high-quality all-microwave qubit gate
abstract: High-fidelity entangling gates are essential for realizing large-scale fault-tolerant superconducting quantum computing, yet existing approaches are limited: frequency-tuning techniques induce decoherence, while all-microwave-driven schemes suffer the trade-off between gate speed and leakage rate. Here, we introduce an energy-level engineering technique that employs the Autler-Townes effect to manipulate the nonlinearity of qubits without perturbing the computational subspace or degrading coherence time. This approach enables an experimentally validated, fast (97 ns) and high-fidelity (99.40(9)%) CZ gate, where error analysis reveals that gate errors arise mainly from static decoherence. The scheme facilitates fast, high-quality all-microwave gate operations with a simple topology and can be applied across various quantum platforms.

title: Symmetry topological field theory for flavor symmetry
abstract: In this work, we demonstrate that the symmetry topological field theory (SymTFT) associated with a quantum field theory (QFT) with continuous non-abelian G -flavor symmetry is a BF -theory with gauge group G . We show that gauging G -symmetry with a flat connection yields a theory with global symmetry characterized by exchanging the conjugate variables in the quantization of BF -theory. We construct the extended operators that generate the G -flavor symmetry and the ( d − 2)-form Rep( G )-symmetry of the gauged QFT. We demonstrate that BF -theory arises as the theory characterizing G -flavor symmetry of a QFT in the AdS/CFT setup.’ t Hooft anomalies of the G -flavor symmetry are realized as extra terms in the action.

title: Charged scalar and Dirac perturbations on a global monopole Reissner-Nordström-de Sitter black hole: Quasinormal modes and strong cosmic censorship
abstract: We study perturbations of charged scalar and Dirac fields around Reissner-Nordström-de Sitter black holes with a global monopole. To this end, we first formulate the equations of motion for both fields on the aforementioned background uniformly in the Teukol-sky equation. Since the Teukolsky equation in asymptotically de Sitter spacetimes can be mapped into the Heun equation, we are then able to solve quasinormal spectra by utilizing the Heun function method, not only for photon sphere modes but also for de Sitter and near-extremal modes. We analyze the spectra of all three types for both fields and, in particular, ascertain the effects of the global monopole. In the near-extremal regime, we find that the presence of a global monopole, on the one hand, leaves the strong cosmic censorship (SCC) conjecture unaffected for scalar perturbations, while on the other hand, it enhances the violation of SCC for Dirac perturbations. Furthermore, we identify that the impact of the global monopole on both the spectra and the SCC is achieved by a shift in the modified multipole number. Our work demonstrates that the Heun function method is an efficient and robust approach for exploring the interaction between asymptotically de Sitter black holes and perturbing fields.

title: Precision spectroscopy via symmetry-protected destructive many-body interferometry
abstract: Precision spectroscopy, a fundamental tool in both fundamental science and practical applications, is inevitably subject to several detrimental effects. Here we propose a symmetry-protected destructive many-body interferometry (SPDMBI) for precision spectroscopy, which successfully mitigates the spectral shifts caused by interparticle interaction, noise, decoherence and experimental imperfection. Through matching the symmetry of the input states and the Hamiltonian, the SPDMBI-based precision spectroscopy yields an antisymmetric spectrum, whose antisymmetric point exactly determines the resonance frequency. In such a precision spectroscopy, the population difference under resonance is always zero, which is a result of the destructive many-body quantum interferometry. To demonstrate its versatility, we showcase successful applications of symmetry-protected Rabi and Ramsey spectroscopy in measuring both time-independent and time-dependent signals. Our protocol improves the performance of precision spectroscopy and offers a pathway for various high-precision quantum sensors.
